stories.title: Agility Robotics now expects to raise about $465 million as it goes public through a SPAC merger
paragraphs: Humanoid robot maker Agility Robotics and Churchill Capital Corp XI said on Oct. 30, 2026 that they expect Agility to raise about $465 million through its proposed merger with the special-purpose acquisition company, The Robot Report reports. According to Agility, that total includes about $164 million from Churchill XI's trust account, about $201 million from a common stock private investment led by Foxconn at $10 per share, and $100 million in equity funding already received after the deal was announced.

The Robot Report notes that the total is less than the $620 million Agility predicted, at a $2.5 billion valuation, when it first announced the planned combination in June. Agility expects the deal to close on Nov. 4, subject to shareholder approval and customary conditions, and said on X that it expects to begin trading on Nasdaq under the ticker AGLT on Nov. 5. The Salem, Oregon company has said it will be the first U.S. publicly traded, pure-play humanoid supplier with commercial deployments.

According to The Robot Report, Agility unveiled its Digit 5 humanoid last month and says it is on track to begin deliveries to early-access customers in the first half of 2027, with general availability targeted for the end of 2027. The company says it has more than $300 million in committed multi-year orders for Digit 5. In a September filing with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission, Agility reported $1.8 million in net sales in 2025, with customers across nine sites including Toyota, Mercado Libre and Schaeffler.

image.credit: Agility Robotics, via The Robot Report

stories.title: AGIBOT shows a third-generation humanoid hardware platform and a new robot foundation model at its Innovation Day in Shanghai
paragraphs: Chinese humanoid robot maker AGIBOT held its AGIBOT Innovation Day 2026 in Shanghai on Oct. 29, 2026, according to the company's posts on X and a report by The Robot Report. AGIBOT introduced Worken, which it describes as a proposed framework for measuring the productive work robots do in real-world settings: the number of active robots, multiplied by their autonomous working hours, multiplied by an output efficiency ratio compared against a reference benchmark for the task.

The company also showed AHA3, its third-generation humanoid hardware architecture, which The Robot Report says adds a joint liquid-cooling system and IP67-rated joints for continuous industrial work. AGIBOT debuted GO-3 Preview, a next-generation robot foundation model built around what it calls a World Reasoning Action Model, and WITA-Omni 1.0, a model for human-robot interaction that combines vision, speech, real-time dialogue and movement.

AGIBOT launched G2 Max, an industrial robot with 21 degrees of freedom and a dual-arm handling capacity of up to 40 kg, and released Link-U OS 1.0, an operating system for embodied AI that it plans to make fully open source by the end of 2026, The Robot Report says. The outlet notes that AGIBOT said last month its 20,000th robot had rolled off the production line, and that IDC reported the company led global humanoid robot shipments in the first half of 2026. No prices or availability dates were given for the new hardware.

image.alt: AGIBOT president and CTO Peng Zhihui introduces Worken on stage at AGIBOT Innovation Day 2026
